name: Storm-1516
keyCapabilities: Credential theft via phishing and unsecured credential gathering (T1552.004)
Backdoor deployment for persistence and lateral movement (GRIMBOLT, SLAYSTYLE, BRICKSTORM, Velociraptor)
Exploitation of zero‑day and public CVEs for initial or privileged access (e.g., CVE-2015‑1701, CVE-2022‑38028, CVE‑2026‑22769, SolarWinds Web Help Desk CVEs)
Wi‑Fi Evil Twin phishing using Wi-Fi Pineapple
Defacement of IoT devices by default manufacturer passwords
Creation and management of >300 fictional media websites to host influence content
Impersonation of legitimate media brands and political movements
Deployment of self-hosted LLM infrastructure for large‑scale disinformation and deepfakes
Use of alternative video platforms (Rumble) and subdomain mirroring for resilience
Targeting of political leaders, elections and critical infrastructure across multiple regions

description: Storm‑1516, also known as CopyCop or Sandworm Team, is a sophisticated Russian state-sponsored actor that blends cyber‑espionage infrastructure deployments with large‑scale political influence campaigns. Its operations target a broad spectrum of critical sectors—including government, finance, energy, and media—across Europe, North America and the Middle East, using credential theft, zero‑day exploits and LLM‑generated disinformation to sow confusion and extract financial value. The actor consistently leverages backdoors, remote management tools and misinformation platforms such as Rumble to maintain persistence and amplify its influence.
goals: The actor’s overarching goal combines financial gain with geopolitical influence. By infiltrating commercial and public sector organizations it can exfiltrate data or leverage stolen credentials for ransom or insider deals. Simultaneously, its media operations aim to destabilize target societies by promoting divisive narratives—particularly against Ukraine—and to erode confidence in democratic institutions. Victims span across governmental ministries, financial services, telecommunications, defense contractors and critical infrastructure operators; the actor prefers high‑visibility targets that can amplify propaganda reach.
